tytul: Chive oil for the refrigerator, used within days (UGA method)
wstep: This card uses the UGA Extension method for oil with non-acidified fresh herbs, here chives: the oil is heated to 180 °F (82 °C) before the herbs are added, and the oil is kept in the refrigerator and thrown away 4 days after it was made, or frozen.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Home-made oils with non-acidified garlic or herbs must never be stored at room temperature.
NCHFP gives the same limit for garlic in oil: make it fresh and keep it in the refrigerator at 40 °F (4.4 °C) or lower for no more than 4 days.

akapity: Vegetables and herbs in oil meet the conditions for botulinum toxin production: spores can be present, oil keeps oxygen out, and the pH is above 4.6.
You cannot tell from the look, smell or taste of the oil whether botulism is a risk.

It covers fresh chives added to heated oil; the acidification method, which allows room-temperature storage, was developed only for garlic, basil, oregano and rosemary and must not be used for chives.
Dried chives do not make the oil safer: without a laboratory measurement nobody knows whether dried herbs are dry enough.
Make only as much oil as you will use within 4 days.
Wash the glass container thoroughly and boil it for 10 minutes.
Choose good-quality chives, wash them thoroughly and pat them dry.
Heat the oil to 180 °F (82 °C), checking it with a kitchen thermometer, and only then add the chives.
Put the oil with the chives into the sterilized container, close it and keep it in the refrigerator.
Throw the oil away 4 days after you made it.
Alternatively, freeze the oil until you are ready to use it.
